producer_report.summary: A drain re-read that ends as needing acceptance now gives its --job-limit slot back. Root cause: run_job takes the slot (st.started += 1) before the re-read, and the needs-accepting arm never returned it. That arm now decrements st.started under the state lock; the re-read cost still counts against the budget. I updated the Limits::max_jobs doc, the --job-limit help in main.rs (the stop-reason table line), and CHANGELOG.md. I added a regression test at max_jobs 1: `a` needs accepting, `b` lands, and the drain does not stop at the job limit. I did not run the revert demonstration myself; the brief leaves it to Athena's recorded revert run.

checks_run.note: 165 passed, including the new test, the_job_limit_stops_the_loop and the existing needs-accepting test
17 passed; the banned-word scan is clean

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`. A new test with max_jobs 1 has item a end as needs accepting and item b runnable. It asserts jobs[0].outcome == "needs accepting", landed == 1 and stop != Stop::JobLimit, and it passes.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`: 165 passed. The new test a_run_that_needs_accepting_does_not_use_up_the_job_limit uses max_jobs 1 and asserts all three.

criteria_check.criterion: Fails without the fix: with the decrement of st.started in the needs-accepting arm of run_job reverted on a scratch copy, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` fails on the new test. The verifier sees this as Athena's recorded revert run under 'Checks Athena ran'.
criteria_check.evidence: I did not run the revert myself; Athena records it. Without the decrement, the slot taken at st.started += 1 stays used. With max_jobs 1, run_job then returns JobLimit for b, so landed would be 0 and the stop JobLimit. The new test's assertions would fail.

criteria_check.criterion: `git diff` of crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs shows the needs-accepting arm in run_job giving the slot back (`st.started` decremented under the state lock). The JobLimit check and the failed, held and passed paths are unchanged.
criteria_check.evidence: The diff adds a block in the `_ if run.needs_accepting` arm: `let mut st = self.st(); st.started = st.started.saturating_sub(1);`. The other edit in drain.rs is a doc comment. No other path is touched.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` still passes the_job_limit_stops_the_loop and the existing needs-accepting tests, and `git diff` shows no removed or weakened asserts.
criteria_check.evidence: All 165 tests pass, including the_job_limit_stops_the_loop and a_run_that_needs_accepting_leaves_the_item_queued_without_a_failure. The test-file change only adds a test; no existing line was removed.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass.

Grep of crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs and crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs for the --job-limit help and the Limits::max_jobs doc finds wording that a re-read that only needs accepting does not count toward the limit. CHANGELOG.md has a matching entry.
criteria_check.evidence: The Limits::max_jobs doc in drain.rs, the --job-limit arg doc and the `job limit` stop-reason line in main.rs all say a re-read that only needs accepting does not count. CHANGELOG.md has a new Fixed entry under Unreleased.

mistakes: My first changelog edit failed because the heading was not unique. I retried with more context.
learnings: The needs-accepting arm of run_job runs after st.started += 1 at the start of run_job, so returning the slot there is the single place to fix it.
The new test copies the Unaccepted stub from the existing needs-accepting test instead of sharing it.
